study_identification_part.si_4_title: Transdiagnostic dimensions of psychopathology explain individuals' unique deviations from normative neurodevelopment in brain structure

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to predict cortical volume values from age and sex. The GPR model provides predicted values, predictive uncertainty, and normative variance, which are combined to create z-score deviations from normative neurodevelopment.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: for each brain region (j), we used gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict cortical volume values from age and sex using the training subset (see ref. 28 for details). An advantage of this approach is that in addition to fitting potentially nonlinear predictions of a brain feature, it also provides regional estimates of the expected variation in the relationship between age and brain features (normative variance) as well as estimates of uncertainty in this variance.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Parkes2021.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical volume was extracted for each of 400 regions defined by the Schaefer atlas. Regional estimates of cortical volume were extracted from participant's native space data using ANTs tools. A sensitivity analysis was also performed using the Lausanne463 parcellation with 463 regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We focused on cortical gray matter, indexed via cortical volume, which is known to undergo plastic maturation in youth. ... cortical volume was extracted for each of 400 regions defined by the Schaefer atlas
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Parkes2021.pdf.md: Introduction; Materials and methods / Normative modeling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as explanatory variables in the normative model to predict cortical volume. The GPR model fitted potentially nonlinear predictions of brain features as a function of age while accounting for sex differences.
